projects.title: Middleman Maze
projects.hook: A farmer drives to market, but every gate takes a bit of the money!
projects.problem: Many farmers lose money to middlemen before food reaches the market. Can you see where the money goes?
learn: Broadcasts: one sprite calls the next one
Events: something happens, then something happens

steps.b: Upload Farmer, Truck, Title and Play Button. Rename each one so you know its job.

steps.t: Hide everything on the green flag
steps.b: Every sprite hides when the flag is clicked. Only Title and PLAY should show.
Click PLAY, then broadcast "trip starts".
Truck drives to gate 1, 2 and 3. At each gate, broadcast "truck reaches gate…".
Make a variable called Money. Reduce it at each gate.
Broadcast "drive to market", then show what the farmer has left.

projects.ask: Ask a market woman: who do you buy from, and how much does the farmer sell it for?
projects.remix: Add a fourth gate, or a gate where a good helper gives money back.

projects.title: Shrinking Naira
projects.hook: Your N1,000 buys less and less each month. Why?
projects.problem: Prices go up, so the same money buys less. This is called inflation. See it happen in a game.
learn: Timers: the market opens and closes

steps.b: Upload Iya Oja, the goods and the Naira note. Rename them. Hide all on green flag.
Stage broadcasts "market opens". Goods appear.
Broadcast "prices go up" every new month. Add to the Price variable.
If the Naira is not enough, broadcast "too expensive".
Iya Oja says the lesson in simple words when you broadcast "show the lesson".
Add a button that freezes the price. What happens to your money?

projects.ask: Ask an older person: how much was a cup of garri when you were my age?
projects.remix: Make the prices rise faster for rice than for yam. Why might that happen?

projects.title: The Empty Barn
projects.hook: The farm is silent. The animals are sick. Can the vaccine save the day?
projects.problem: Sick animals mean no food and no money. Vaccines protect a farm.
learn: Sunset: a timer for the day

steps.b: Upload farmer, animals, vaccine box and barn backdrop. Rename. Hide on the green flag.
Broadcast "farm day starts" from PLAY.
Broadcast "farmer explains". Farmer says why the barn is empty.
Clicking the vaccine box broadcasts "vaccine heals the sick".
Switch costume from sick to healthy.
Broadcast "sunset comes", then "farmer gives the result".

projects.ask: Ask: what does a vet do? What would a farmer do if there was no vet?
projects.remix: Add a second sickness with a different medicine. Only the right one should heal.

projects.title: Honest Scale
projects.hook: You sell at a market stall. Cheat the customer and they stop coming back!
projects.problem: Fair weight builds trust. Cheating gives quick money but loses customers.

steps.b: Upload seller, customers, scale and Mama T. Rename. Hide on green flag.
Broadcast "show the order". The customer says what they want.
Player clicks the scale. Broadcast "start weighing".
If you give full weight, broadcast "customer got full weight". If you cheat, "customer was cheated".
Full weight: Trust goes up. Cheated: Trust goes down.
At the end, broadcast "mama t checks trust". Say the result.

projects.ask: Ask a seller: what makes you buy from the same person again and again?
projects.remix: Add a rival stall with an honest neighbour who gets your customers.

projects.title: Real vs Fake
projects.hook: Two products look the same. Only one is real. Can you spot it?
projects.problem: Fake products can harm people. Spotting small details keeps you safe.

steps.b: Upload rice, milk, noodles, tomato paste and the explainer. Rename. Hide on green flag.
Broadcast "show rice" (then milk, noodles, tomato paste).
Clicking the fake broadcasts "fake found". Clicking the real one broadcasts "real one tapped".
Broadcast "explain rice" so the explainer shows the clue.
Broadcast "hide rice", then show the next product.
After the last product, or when lives run out, broadcast "game over".

missions.t: Use a variable for lives or score

projects.ask: Look at a real tin of tomato paste at home. What 3 details prove it is real?
projects.remix: Add a magnifier sprite that follows the mouse and shows a clue.

projects.title: Family Job Board
projects.hook: Tayo has chores to do before Daddy comes home. Pick the right chore!
projects.problem: Helping at home teaches responsibility. Doing chores in the right order saves time.

steps.b: Upload Tayo, the chore pictures and Daddy. Rename. Hide on green flag.
Broadcast "chore 1" to "chore 4". Each chore glows.
Right chore: broadcast "right chore". Wrong one: "wrong chore".
Tayo sweeps, fetches water, washes plates, washes clothes. Use a different broadcast for each.
Broadcast "chores done".
Broadcast "daddy comes home" and Daddy gives a medal.

projects.ask: Ask: which chore at home takes the longest? Which one is the quickest?
projects.remix: Give a 40-second clock. Beat the clock to earn Gold.

projects.title: Naira Wise
projects.hook: Ada gets pocket money. Spend, save, or share? The jars decide!
projects.problem: Learning to split money early builds good habits for life.

steps.b: Upload Ada, Mum, three jars and the storybook. Rename. Hide on green flag.
Broadcast "mum gives pocket money". Money variable goes up.
Start the clock with "jars and 10 second clock start". Click a jar to put money in.
When the clock ends, broadcast "time is up". Leftover money disappears!
Broadcast "sandal breaks". Do you have savings to fix it?
Broadcast "new week starts". Check after 3 weeks.

projects.ask: Ask your mum: what is one thing you saved for? How long did it take?
projects.remix: Let the player choose how many seconds they get.

projects.title: Race Against Rot
projects.hook: Tomatoes go bad fast. Get them to market before they rot!
projects.problem: A lot of food is wasted before it is sold. Good storage and fast transport save money.

steps.b: Upload farmer, tomatoes, truck, buyer and storage cards. Rename. Hide on green flag.
Broadcast "show storage cards". Player picks one.
Make a Freshness variable that goes down every second.
Broadcast "drive to market". Truck moves.
The buyer pays more if Freshness is high. Broadcast "buyer pays".
Farmer checks the money and says what helped most.

projects.ask: Ask: how do people keep tomatoes fresh without a fridge?
projects.remix: Add rain that makes the road slower.

projects.title: The Great Owambe Budget
projects.hook: Plan a big party with a small budget. Pick, un-pick, and beware of debt!
projects.problem: Parties cost a lot. A budget stops you from spending more than you have.

steps.b: Upload host, food, music, tent and the lender. Rename. Hide on green flag.
Broadcast "start planning". Show the choices with prices.
Click once to add. Click again to remove.
If the total is more than the budget, broadcast "too expensive".
Broadcast "lender gives loan". Money goes up, but now you owe more.
Broadcast "monday comes", then "check for debt". Does the host explain well?

projects.ask: Ask an adult who planned a party: what did they forget to count?
projects.remix: Add Aunty's surprise: a guest who brings extra friends.

projects.title: Scam Shield
projects.hook: A strange message says "You won N500,000!" Is it real or a scam?
projects.problem: Scam messages trick people out of money. Scam Shield helps people spot the signs.
learn: Buttons and forms make a site do things

steps.b: Open the live Scam Shield. Test 3 things on it.
Find the heading, a button, a picture and a link. Draw them on paper.
Write 5 signs of a scam message you learnt.
On the Web path, build a page with a heading and a warning box.

projects.ask: Show your parents a scam message example. Can they tell?
projects.remix: Make a "Safe or Scam?" card for your own street.

projects.title: Harvest Calendar Naija
projects.hook: What do you plant in which month? A calendar for Nigerian farmers.
projects.problem: Planting at the wrong time wastes seeds. A good calendar helps farmers plan.
learn: Colours make things easy to read

steps.b: Look at it. Which month has the most crops?
Find the menu, the month list and a crop card.
Ask: what do you plant at the start of the rainy season?
Build a card for one crop with a name, month and tip.

missions.t: Make a crop card on paper

projects.ask: Ask a farmer or an elder: which crop is easiest to grow where you live?
projects.remix: Add your own local crop to the calendar idea.

projects.title: Apprentice Pathway Explorer
projects.hook: Not every great job needs a university. Explore trades and apprenticeships!
projects.problem: Many young people do not know the trades they can learn. This site shows the paths.
learn: Filters help you find what you want

steps.b: Click on 3 different trades.
Write one thing that is the same and one that is different.
Ask: how did you learn it?
Draw a card for one trade with a photo, name and 3 facts.

projects.ask: Ask a tailor, a mechanic or a baker: how did you start?
projects.remix: Plan a filter button: show only trades you can start at 15.

projects.title: Community Voice AI
projects.hook: Turn a problem in your street into a clear, polite letter!
projects.problem: Many people do not know how to write a formal letter. The AI helps them be heard.
learn: AI needs good facts from you
You must check what AI writes

steps.b: Type a small problem, like a blocked drain.
Is it polite? Is anything wrong or made-up?
Add who, where and since when. See the difference.
Fix one thing the AI got wrong.

projects.ask: Ask: what problem in our community needs a letter?
projects.remix: Plan a version for a school problem.

projects.title: Inflation Explainer AI
projects.hook: Ask: "Why is rice so expensive?" and get a simple answer.
projects.problem: Inflation is hard to understand. An AI can explain it in kid words.
learn: AI can be wrong, so check

steps.b: Ask it one question about prices.
Ask it to explain like you are 10.
Ask an adult if the answer is right.
Make it short and clear.

projects.ask: Ask an adult: what costs more now than last year?
projects.remix: Plan a version that explains prices for a seller.

projects.title: Naija Career Compass AI
projects.hook: Tell it what you like, and it points to jobs you might love.
projects.problem: Students pick jobs they have only heard of. A compass shows more paths.
learn: Choose with your family and teachers

steps.b: Type 3 things you like.
Which one surprised you?
Which school subjects does it need?
Which idea fits you? Why?

missions.t: Find a job that surprised you

projects.ask: Ask 3 adults: what job do you do, and what do you love about it?
projects.remix: Plan a quiz that asks what you like first.

projects.title: Danfo World Tour
projects.hook: A yellow danfo bus drives from Lagos to Cairo, Paris and Tokyo!
projects.problem: See how backdrops, a moving bus and messages make a travel animation.

steps.b: Pick or draw a yellow danfo. Name it Bus.
Add Lagos, Cairo, Paris and Tokyo backdrops.
Glide the bus across the screen.
At the edge, broadcast "next city" and switch the backdrop.
Bus says hello in a local word each time.
After Tokyo, say "We did it!"

missions.t: Move the bus with glide or move

projects.ask: Ask: which of these four cities would you visit first? Why?
projects.remix: Add a border check where the bus waits 2 seconds.

projects.title: Ankara Pattern Maker
projects.hook: Draw colourful patterns with just a few blocks and a loop.
projects.problem: Famous cloth patterns repeat. Computers love repeating!

steps.b: Click the extension button (bottom-left) and add Pen.
Pen down, repeat 4: move 80, turn 90.
Repeat 36: draw the square, then turn 10.
Add "change pen colour by 10" inside the loop.
Press space to draw a new pattern.
Use the stamp to make a cloth with many patterns.

projects.ask: Look at a cloth at home. What shape repeats?
projects.remix: Add a second pattern for Japanese waves.

projects.title: Water Walk
projects.hook: Carry water home without spilling. Dodge the stones!
projects.problem: In many places, children walk far for clean water. Make a game that shows the journey.

steps.b: Pick a girl with a bucket and a path backdrop.
Left and right arrows move her.
A stone moves down. If touching, lose 1 litre.
Make a variable Litres. Start at 10.
Reach home with litres above 0 to win.
Add a message at the end about clean water.

projects.ask: Ask: where does your house get its water from?
projects.remix: Make the stones move faster each round.

projects.title: Talking Drum Beats
projects.hook: Press keys to play a talking drum and a Japanese taiko together.
projects.problem: Rhythm is a pattern of sounds. Patterns are maths!

steps.b: Add two drum sprites.
Click a drum to play a sound.
A key plays the drum too.
Repeat 4: play, wait 0.5.
Change costume when you play.
Play a beat and show your friends.

projects.ask: Clap a beat to a friend. Can they copy it?
projects.remix: Mix a second rhythm from another country.

projects.title: Rain Rescue Farmer
projects.hook: Heavy rain! Catch the falling seeds before they wash away.
projects.problem: Floods can wash seeds away. Catch what you can.

steps.b: Add a farmer who follows the mouse left and right.
Add a seed that falls from the top.
If touching the farmer, add 1 to Score.
When it hits the ground, go back to the top.
Play a rain sound.
At 10 points, say "You saved the farm!"

projects.ask: Ask: what do farmers do when too much rain falls?
projects.remix: Add a basket that grows when you do well.

projects.title: One Story, Four Countries
projects.hook: The same clever animal story told in Nigeria, Ghana, Japan and Brazil.
projects.problem: Stories travel the world and change shape. Animation can show it.

steps.b: Choose a short story you know.
One backdrop for each country.
Add one animal and one friend.
Animal says a line. Broadcast to the friend. Friend replies.
Switch the backdrop each time.
Show a message about what the story teaches.

projects.ask: Ask a grandparent for a story they were told as a child.
projects.remix: Add your own country and your own animal.

projects.title: Plastic to Treasure
projects.hook: Sort rubbish into the right bin and watch plastic turn into treasure.
projects.problem: Plastic blocks drains and causes floods. Sorting helps recycling.

steps.b: Add Plastic, Paper and Food bins.
Pick an item. It says what it is.
If the item matches the bin, add 1 point.
Say "Try again". No point.
Switch costume to the next item.
At 5 points, turn plastic into a toy or bag.

projects.ask: Look in your bin at home. How much is plastic?
projects.remix: Add a bin for glass or metal.

projects.title: Safe Crossing
projects.hook: Cross the busy road only when the light says it is safe.
projects.problem: Road accidents hurt many children. Waiting at the right time saves lives.

steps.b: A road, a child and a light.
Forever: red for 5 seconds, then green.
Cars glide across when the light is red.
Press up to cross.
If the light is red and you cross, say "Danger!"
Say "Safe!" and add a point.

projects.ask: Look at the road near your school. Where is the safest place to cross?
projects.remix: Add a zebra crossing that makes cars stop.

projects.title: Space Jollof
projects.hook: A Naija astronaut blasts off with a pot of jollof. Count down 3, 2, 1!
projects.problem: A rocket launch is an easy first animation. Count, move, and spin.

steps.b: Add a rocket and a space backdrop.
Say 3… 2… 1… Go! with waits.
Switch costume to show flames.
Glide the rocket up the screen.
Show a pot of jollof floating.
Say "Best jollof in space!"

projects.ask: Ask: if you took one food to space, what would it be?
projects.remix: Add a second planet to visit.

projects.title: Hello World Translator
projects.hook: Ask for a word and say it in Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, French and Swahili.
projects.problem: Speaking many languages brings people together.

steps.b: Ask "Type hello, thanks or water".
If answer = hello, say hello in 5 languages.
Do the same for thanks and water.
If no word matches, say "I do not know that one yet."
Show a sprite for each language.
Forever ask again.

projects.ask: Ask a friend how to say "thank you" in their language.
projects.remix: Add a language from your own family.

projects.title: Blackout Treasure Hunt
projects.hook: NEPA took the light! Find 3 hidden treasures before power returns.
projects.problem: Make a dark scene with a torch that follows your mouse.

steps.b: A room backdrop with a dark cover.
A torch sprite goes to the mouse.
Treasures are hidden. When the torch touches, they show.
Variable Found goes up by 1.
After 30 seconds, "Power is back!"
If Found is 3 before time ends, say "You win!"

projects.ask: Ask: what do you do at home when there is no light?
projects.remix: Add a second room.

projects.title: Penalty Shootout: Naija vs the World
projects.hook: Aim, shoot, and beat the keeper! Who will win the cup?
projects.problem: Football is played everywhere. Random numbers make the keeper hard to beat.

steps.b: Pitch backdrop, ball, keeper.
Left or right arrow picks the corner.
Keeper picks a random corner.
If same corner, saved. If not, goal.
Two variables: You and Keeper.
Show a trophy.

projects.ask: Ask: who is your favourite player? Why?
projects.remix: Add a crowd that cheers.

projects.title: Four-Colour Champion
projects.hook: Make ONE game that uses all four logic colours. Your term goal!
projects.problem: Real programmers mix everything: variables, conditions, loops, and events.

steps.b: Choose a simple idea you love.
Score, lives, or money.
An if / else that changes what happens.
A forever loop or a timer.
Broadcast to start and end the game.
Ask a friend to find one bug.

projects.ask: Ask a friend: what game would you love to play? Build part of it.
projects.remix: Add a title screen and a play button.

projects.title: My Passport to the World
projects.hook: Make a web page that is your own passport. Stamp the countries you dream of!
projects.problem: Every website starts with a page. A passport page is a fun way to learn the frame and the tags.
learn: The page frame: head and body

steps.b: The <title> goes in the head. It shows on the browser tab.
<h1> is the biggest heading. Put your name in it.
<ul> makes a list. Each country is an <li>.
<a href="https://..."> makes a link people can tap.

missions.t: Make a list with at least 3 <li> countries.

projects.ask: Ask 3 friends: which country would you visit first? Why?
projects.remix: Add a second list: foods from each country.

lab.starter:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <!-- 1: add a <title> -->

</head>
<body>
  <!-- 2: add an <h1> with your name -->

  <!-- 3: add a list (ul) with 3 countries (li) -->

  <!-- 4: add a link (a) to a website -->

</body>
</html>
lab.solution:
Passport of Ada

Countries I want to visit:

  • Japan
  • Brazil
  • Egypt
Read about the world

missions.say: Put a <title> in the <head>.
Add an <h1> with your name.
Make a list with at least 3 <li> countries.
missions.hint: Use <ul>, then one <li> for each country.
missions.test: return t.count('ul > li')>=3 && t.all('ul > li').every(function(l){return l.textContent.trim().length>1})

missions.say: Add a link with <a href="...">.

projects.title: Jollof Meets the World
projects.hook: Write a recipe card for jollof and a dish from another country.
projects.problem: Recipes are lists in a clear order. HTML has special tags for steps.

steps.b: <h2> makes a smaller heading. Use one for each dish.
<ol> numbers the steps. Each step is an <li>.
<strong> makes words bold.

missions.t: Add an <ol> with 3 or more steps.
Add a second <h2> for a dish from another country.

projects.ask: Ask: what is the best dish in your family? What goes in it?
projects.remix: Add the dish from your own grandmother.

lab.starter: Jollof Meets the World
lab.solution:
Jollof Meets the World

Naija Jollof

  1. Fry the pepper and onions.
  2. Add rice and stock.
  3. Cook on low heat.

Japanese Onigiri

Rice balls with a tasty filling.

missions.say: Add an <h2> for your jollof.
Add an <ol> with 3 or more steps.
Make some words bold with <strong>.
Add a second <h2> for a dish from another country.

projects.title: Birthday Card for Mama
projects.hook: Make a bright birthday card page with CSS. Colours make people smile!
projects.problem: HTML is the skeleton. CSS is the clothes. It makes pages beautiful.

steps.b: background-color changes the page colour.
text-align: center puts it in the middle.
font-size: 40px makes big words.
color changes text colour.

missions.t: Give the body a background colour.
Make the h1 at least 40px big.
Give the h1 a colour that is not black.

projects.ask: Ask your mum her favourite colour. Use it!
projects.remix: Add a second message and style it too.

lab.starter:
Happy Birthday, Mama!

You are the best.
lab.solution:
Happy Birthday, Mama!

You are the best.

missions.say: Give the body a background colour.
Centre the h1.
Make the h1 at least 40px big.
Give the h1 a colour that is not black.

projects.title: Ankara Colour Cards
projects.hook: Make three colourful cards in a row, like cloth patterns.
projects.problem: Designers place things in rows and columns. Flexbox does this easily.

steps.b: Give each card class="card".
display: flex on the parent puts children side by side.
border-radius makes soft corners.
Give each card its own background colour.

missions.t: Round the corners of .card (8px or more).
Give each card its own background colour.

projects.ask: Look at a real ankara cloth. Which 3 colours do you see?
projects.remix: Add a fourth card for another language.

lab.starter:
Yoruba
Igbo
Hausa
lab.solution:
Yoruba
Igbo
Hausa

missions.say: Make .row a flex row.
Round the corners of .card (8px or more).
Give each card its own background colour.
Keep all 3 cards.

projects.title: Clean Water Poster
projects.hook: Design a hero banner that tells people why clean water matters.
projects.problem: Good websites start with a strong first screen. We call it the hero.

steps.b: Give the hero a background colour and padding.
Make the heading large and white.
Add a <button> people can tap.
a :hover rule changes the button when touched.

missions.t: Give .hero at least 30px padding on top.
Make the h1 white and at least 28px.

projects.ask: Ask: where does water come from in your area?
projects.remix: Add a counter: "2 in 10 children need clean water" (ask your teacher for a real number).

lab.starter:
Clean water for every child

One tap can change a village.
lab.solution:
Clean water for every child

One tap can change a village.

missions.say: Give .hero a background colour.
Give .hero at least 30px padding on top.
Make the h1 white and at least 28px.
Add a button:hover rule.

projects.title: Phone-Friendly Menu
projects.hook: Build a menu that looks right on a phone AND on a computer.
projects.problem: Most Nigerian users are on phones. A good site must fit small screens.

steps.b: A <nav> with links. Flex puts them in a row.
@media (max-width: 600px) changes the layout on phones.
flex-direction: column stacks links.

missions.t: Put the menu links in a row on a big screen.
Stack the links in a column on a phone (360px).

projects.ask: Open a website on your phone. Does the menu change shape?
projects.remix: Add a fourth link and a logo.

lab.starter:
• Home
  • Games
  • About
lab.solution:
• Home
  • Games
  • About

missions.say: Put the menu links in a row on a big screen.
missions.test: return await t.at(900,function(){return t.css('nav ul','display')==='flex' && t.css('nav ul','flex-direction')==='row'})

missions.say: Add an @media rule.
Stack the links in a column on a phone (360px).
missions.hint: Inside the media rule: nav ul { flex-direction: column; }

missions.say: Keep the 3 links.
missions.hint: Do not delete Home, Games and About.

projects.title: Market Total Calculator
projects.hook: Type a price and how many. The page does the sum for you!
projects.problem: Traders add many prices every day. A calculator saves time and mistakes.

steps.b: document.getElementById("price").value gives what the user typed.
Multiply price by quantity. Use Number() to change text to a number.
Put the result in the page with textContent.
If nothing is typed, show a friendly message.

missions.t: 20 naira x 2 should show 40 (new numbers, new answer).
Empty boxes show a friendly message.

projects.ask: Ask a trader: what do you add up the most every day?
projects.remix: Add a discount box that takes 10% off.

lab.starter: Market Total
lab.solution: Market Total

missions.say: 50 naira x 3 should show 150.
20 naira x 2 should show 40 (new numbers, new answer).
missions.hint: Do not write 150 in the code. Let the maths work.

missions.say: Empty boxes show a friendly message.
Try 7 x 3. It should show 21.
missions.hint: Let the maths work for ANY numbers.

projects.title: Day and Night Switch
projects.hook: A button that flips your page between day and night mode!
projects.problem: Dark mode helps eyes at night and saves phone battery.
learn: CSS classes that change the look

steps.b: In CSS write .night { background: #111; color: white; }.
Use document.getElementById.
document.body.classList.toggle("night") switches it.
Say "Go to day" or "Go to night".

missions.t: Add a body.night (or .night) rule in CSS.
Clicking the button gives the body the class night.
The page background really changes to dark.
Click again to go back to day.

projects.ask: Ask: do you like dark mode on your phone? Why?
projects.remix: Add a third mode: Nigerian green.

lab.starter: Hello, world
lab.solution: Hello, world

missions.say: Add a body.night (or .night) rule in CSS.
Clicking the button gives the body the class night.
The page background really changes to dark.
Click again to go back to day.

projects.title: Which Country? Quiz
projects.hook: A one-question quiz that says "Correct!" or "Try again".
projects.problem: Quizzes teach by asking. They use if / else, just like Scratch.

steps.b: Each answer is a <button>.
Use an if to check.
Show Correct! or Try again.

missions.t: Use if and else in answer().

projects.ask: Ask a friend a question about your country and add it.
projects.remix: Add a score that goes up for every right answer.

lab.starter: Which country has the city of Lagos?
lab.solution: Which country has the city of Lagos?

missions.say: Clicking Nigeria shows Correct!
Clicking Ghana shows Try again.
Clicking Kenya shows Try again.
Use if and else in answer().

projects.title: Language Greeter
projects.hook: Pick a language from a menu and the page says hello in it.
projects.problem: Real apps look things up in a list. In JavaScript the list is an object.

steps.b: A <select> with <option> choices.
var hello = { yoruba: "Bawo ni", ... }
hello[select.value] gives the greeting.

projects.ask: Ask a friend to teach you hello in their language.
projects.remix: Add a fifth language from your family.

lab.starter: Say hello
lab.solution: Say hello

missions.say: Choosing Yoruba shows Bawo ni.
Choosing Igbo shows Kedu.
Choosing Hausa shows Sannu.
Choosing French shows Bonjour.

projects.title: Good Habit Tracker
projects.hook: Add habits to a list and tick them off. Like a real app!
projects.problem: Apps that help people build habits (like washing hands) use lists you can add to.

steps.b: Read the input and make a new <li>.
list.appendChild(li) adds it.
Clicking an item adds the class "done".
After adding, set input.value = "".

missions.t: Typing a habit and pressing Add puts it in the list.
The input box clears after adding.
Clicking a habit gives it the class done.

projects.ask: Ask your family: what is one good habit that helps you?
projects.remix: Add a delete button next to each habit.

lab.starter: My good habits
lab.solution: My good habits

missions.say: Typing a habit and pressing Add puts it in the list.
missions.hint: Create an li and appendChild it.
missions.test: t.type('#habit','wash hands');await t.click('#add');return t.count('#list li')===1 && /wash hands/.test(t.text('#list li'))

missions.say: Empty input adds nothing.
The input box clears after adding.
Clicking a habit gives it the class done.

puzzles.script:
when green flag clicked
hide
say [Hello!] for (2) seconds
puzzles.q: What happens when you click the green flag?
o: The sprite says Hello for 2 seconds, then hides
puzzles.why: Blocks run from top to bottom. It hides first. The say block is below, but a hidden sprite cannot be seen.

puzzles.script:
when this sprite clicked
change [score v] by (1)
puzzles.q: What does clicking this sprite do?
puzzles.why: 'change score by 1' adds one each time.

puzzles.script:
when green flag clicked
forever
move (10) steps
if on edge, bounce
end
puzzles.q: What will the sprite do?
o: Keep moving and bounce at the edges
puzzles.why: Forever means it never stops. If on edge, bounce turns it round.

puzzles.script:
when I receive [start v]
show
say [Welcome!] for (2) seconds
puzzles.q: When does this script run?
o: When the green flag is clicked
puzzles.why: 'When I receive' waits for a broadcast message. It is the purple events colour.

puzzles.script:
when green flag clicked
set [lives v] to (3)
repeat (3)
change [lives v] by (-1)
end
puzzles.q: What is the value of lives at the end?
puzzles.why: Start at 3, take away 1 three times, and you get 0.

puzzles.script:
when green flag clicked
if <(score) > (9)> then
say [You win!]
else
say [Keep going!]
end
puzzles.q: Score is 5. What does the sprite say?
puzzles.why: 5 is not more than 9, so the else part runs.

puzzles.script:
when green flag clicked
set [money v] to (100)
change [money v] by (-30)
change [money v] by (-30)
puzzles.q: How much money is left?

puzzles.script:
when this sprite clicked
broadcast [next scene v]
hide
puzzles.q: What does this script do?
o: Tells other sprites 'next scene', then hides
puzzles.why: Top to bottom: broadcast first, then hide.

puzzles.script:
when green flag clicked
set [time v] to (10)
repeat until <(time) = (0)>
wait (1) seconds
change [time v] by (-1)
end
broadcast [time is up v]
puzzles.q: How long does this take, and what happens at the end?
o: 10 seconds, then 'time is up' is sent
puzzles.why: It waits 1 second 10 times. When time is 0, the loop stops and 'time is up' is sent.

puzzles.title: Make a title screen
puzzles.why: Start with the green flag. Then hide, wait, show, and say.

puzzles.title: A sprite that starts a game when clicked
puzzles.why: The sprite is clicked, hides, then tells everyone.

puzzles.title: Count down from 3
puzzles.why: First set the number. Then repeat the change.

puzzles.title: Catch game score
puzzles.why: Set score to 0 first. Then keep checking if the basket is touched.

puzzles.title: Ask and answer
blocks: ask [What is your name?] and wait
puzzles.why: Ask first. The answer only exists after you ask.

puzzles.title: This sprite should hide when the game starts. Which block is wrong?
puzzles.why: The sprite should hide on the flag, but 'show' makes it appear.

puzzles.title: Click the sprite to add 1 point. Which block is wrong?
puzzles.why: -1 takes a point away. It should be +1.

puzzles.title: This should send a message when time is up. Which block is wrong?
puzzles.why: It should broadcast 'time is up', not 'start'.

puzzles.title: The game must start with 3 lives. Which block is wrong?
puzzles.why: Lives should be 3. Starting at 0 means you lose straight away.

puzzles.title: The sprite should move right when you press the right arrow. Which block is wrong?
puzzles.why: Right means a positive x. -10 moves left.

puzzles.q: What colour are variable blocks in our guide?
puzzles.why: Variables are blue. They remember things like score and money.

puzzles.q: What does a variable do?
puzzles.why: A variable is like a box with a name that stores something.

puzzles.q: Which colour is for 'if / else' choices in our guide?
puzzles.why: Conditionals (choices) are red.

puzzles.q: A 'forever' block is…
puzzles.why: Loops repeat. Forever never ends until you press stop.

puzzles.q: What does 'broadcast' do?
o: Sends a message to all sprites
puzzles.why: Sprites that wait with 'when I receive' hear the message and act.

puzzles.q: Which hat block starts a script when the flag is clicked?
puzzles.why: The green flag is the start button of your game.

puzzles.q: What happens to a hidden sprite?
o: It is invisible but still there
puzzles.why: Hide just makes it invisible. You can show it again.

puzzles.q: Which block repeats something exactly 10 times?
puzzles.why: Repeat counts. Forever never stops.

puzzles.q: What is the best use for a timer?
puzzles.why: A timer or wait helps with time limits.

puzzles.q: Why do we use broadcasts?
puzzles.why: One sprite tells the others when to act. It keeps your code tidy.

puzzles.q: If score = 5 and you 'change score by 2', what is the score now?
A costume is…
o: Another picture of the same sprite
puzzles.why: Switching costumes makes a sprite look like it is moving.

puzzles.q: You want a sprite to follow the mouse. Which block helps?
puzzles.why: 'go to mouse-pointer' inside a forever loop follows the mouse.

puzzles.q: How do you make a different random number each time?
puzzles.why: Random picks a new number each time it runs.

puzzles.q: What does HTML do?
puzzles.why: HTML is the skeleton: headings, text, pictures and links.

puzzles.q: What does CSS do?
puzzles.why: CSS gives colour, size and space.

puzzles.q: What does JavaScript do?
puzzles.why: JavaScript is for buttons that react, scores that change, and more.

puzzles.q: Which tag makes the biggest heading?
puzzles.why: h1 is the main heading. h6 is the smallest.

puzzles.q: Which tag shows a picture?
puzzles.why: shows a picture.

puzzles.q: A link in HTML is made with…
puzzles.why: Click me is a link.

puzzles.q: In CSS, what does color: red; change?
puzzles.why: color changes the text colour. background changes the background.

puzzles.q: Which is a safe password?
o: A long mix of words, numbers and symbols
puzzles.why: Long and mixed passwords are hard to guess.

puzzles.q: What does a browser do?
puzzles.why: Chrome and Safari are browsers.

puzzles.q: What does 'responsive' mean?
o: The page fits big and small screens
puzzles.why: A responsive page works on phones and computers.

puzzles.q: What is a prompt?
puzzles.why: A prompt is your question or instruction to the AI.

puzzles.q: Which prompt is better?
o: Write 5 simple lines about farming in Ogun State for a 10-year-old
puzzles.why: Clear instructions get clearer answers.

puzzles.q: AI sometimes gets facts wrong. What do you do?
o: Check with a trusted adult or book
puzzles.why: Always check important facts.

puzzles.q: Is it safe to type your home address into an AI app?
puzzles.why: Never share private details like your address, school or phone number.

puzzles.q: Who owns the work if AI draws a picture for you?
o: Say you drew it by hand
puzzles.why: Be honest about AI help. Honesty is part of being a good creator.

puzzles.q: An AI says something unkind. What do you do?
puzzles.why: Tell a trusted adult.

puzzles.q: What does an AI need to give a good answer?
o: Clear facts and a clear goal
puzzles.why: Say who, what, and why.

puzzles.q: What is a good first step when AI writes your homework?
o: Read it, check it, and make it yours
puzzles.why: AI is a helper, not the boss. You must understand it.
